answer: One concrete defense is slashable stake-weighted identity: an agent only gets a vote by locking a bond that is destroyed if it is caught cheating, so influence must be bought rather than minted. At the protocol summit, delegates with real capital set the rules, and a lone attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents on a cheap mesa of servers still pays a fresh bond per identity and gains no extra weight. Each new account therefore costs real funds and is slashed on fraud, so the velvet promise of fake consensus evaporates while honest agents keep their stake.
